title: Does a tiny always-on keyword model that wakes a bigger one beat the best single model on energy?
lede: classifier-only energy of two-stage keyword-spotting cascades vs 40 single MLPs retrained on the original Speech Commands v0.02 (5 seeds, 200 models, about 41,000 cascades per seed, thresholds chosen on validation): cascades cut modelled energy by 0 to 28% at the same validation target, losing 0.3 to 1.4 test points, and the saving is under 1% of a system whose MFCC front end costs about 50 times the classifier
summary: Track 8 asked whether co-design beats pairing the best model with a generic engine; this project asks a runtime version: does a small model that answers confident clips and escalates unsure ones to a bigger model beat the best single model? It retrains the accel-kws grid (segments 7/12, hidden 8 to 128, weights 2/3/4/8 bits; 40 integer models) on the original Speech Commands v0.02 tarball with its own speaker-disjoint splits (33,895 / 4,084 / 4,509 clips), 5 seeds. Per seed, every ordered small/big pair is a cascade (about 41,000 per seed), escalating when the small model's integer logit margin is below a threshold chosen on validation only. Energy is the classifier's modelled MAC energy (constants checked against Horowitz 2014 in accel-horowitzcheck) plus the escalated fraction of the big model. At validation targets of 0.65 to 0.74 the cheapest cascade uses 0.73 to 0.98 of the cheapest single model's energy (mean ratios 0.82, 0.98, 0.73, 0.77 at 0.65, 0.70, 0.72, 0.74; 0.92 and 0.98 at 0.55 and 0.60 where only some seeds benefit), but its test accuracy is 0.3 to 1.4 points lower (test-set standard error about 0.7 points). The best single model reaches 0.755 test. Limits: classifier energy only; accel-frontend found the MFCC front end draws about 50 times the classifier, which swamps any cascade saving; clips are isolated words, not a stream dominated by silence; modelled, not measured, energy; one hidden layer; unknown class subsampled.
